summary: This page serves as the Table of Contents for the Lendlease REIT annual report, outlining sections including Group Overview, Performance Overview, Governance, Financial Statements, and Other Information. No schema-relevant data such as audited Portfolio Statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present on this page.

This page presents the Performance Highlights for the SGX REIT, featuring a DPU table showing FY2025 distribution of $3.60 per unit alongside gross revenue ($206.5m), total assets ($3,906.2m), and distributable income ($87.6m) reported in SGD'm. The section also includes financial highlights on capital management such as a 42.6% gearing ratio and weighted average cost of debt of 3.46%, along with trade/tenant mix details indicating rental reversion percentages for retail (10.2%), office (13%), and Jem office (1.7%).

This page of the Lendlease REIT annual report focuses on strategic priorities and portfolio performance, highlighting a transaction to divest the Jem office component completed on 4 August 2025 to reduce gearing to approximately 35% on a proforma basis. It explicitly presents key financial highlights including achieved retail rental reversion of 10.2% and 99.5% occupancy for the retail portfolio, alongside management commentary on interest rate hedging strategies and operational initiatives such as refreshing tenant mixes with new brands like Casa Vostra and Lululemon.

This page presents corporate information for the SGX REIT JYEU, including manager details (Lendlease Global Commercial Trust Management Pte. Ltd.), trustee (DBS Trustee Limited), board composition, committee memberships, auditor (KPMG LLP), and unit registrar (Boardroom Corporate & Advisory Services Pte. Ltd.). No schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present on this page.

This page displays the Appraised Portfolio Value of S\$3.76 billion and Retail Rental Reversion of 10.2% as key performance indicators within the Performance Overview section, which indexes subsequent reports on Operations Review, Property Summary, Financial Review, Independent Market Review, and Investor Relations.

This page presents the **Operations Review** with a top-N property type and location mix table showing Suburban retail/office (61%), Prime retail (28%), Grade A commercial buildings (11%), Singapore (11%), and Milan (89%) alongside key operational metrics in SGD'000, including Retail Committed Occupancy at 99.5% and Office Committed Occupancy at 86.6%. It details strategic asset recycling via the S\$462 million divestment of Jem office as of 30 June 2025 and highlights retail-led performance with a 10.2% rental reversion and new tenant introductions across core markets.

This page presents the Portfolio Occupancy table (showing 92.1% as at 30 Jun 2025), the Lease Expiry Profile table (detailing expiry percentages by NLA and GRI from FY2026 to FY2030+), and the Trade Sector Breakdown table (listing sector distribution by NLA).
This page presents an Operations Review featuring a Trade Sector Breakdown table by GRI, Top-N tenant tables (by GRI and NLA), and tables detailing Tenant Sales and Shopper Traffic in S$ million.

The page features an **audited Portfolio Statement (property valuations)** table detailing Lendlease REIT's portfolio valuation as of 30 June 2025 at S$3,763.3 million, reporting values in SGD'000 with a year-on-year increase of 2.2% supported by the Jem and 313@somerset assets. The text also describes asset enhancement works carried out on Building 3 and Jem to improve tenant experience and preserve long-term asset value within the resilient Singapore market context.

This page presents a property summary for Jem Singapore featuring a Key Statistics table that explicitly names the Gross Revenue for FY2025 as S$129.8 million and Net Property Income for FY2025 as S$94.1 million, alongside details on net lettable area, ownership, and valuation.

This page presents a **Trade Sector Breakdown by GRI** table and chart, listing 16 sectors with Food & Beverages as the largest at 26.6%, alongside a **Lease Expiry Profile by NLA and GRI (%)** table for fiscal years FY2026 to FY2030 and beyond. No audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements, gross revenue notes, top-N tenants, trade/tenant mix, distribution highlights, or manager/trustee/sponsor information are present; however, a map of the Jurong East area is included showing various facilities and landmarks.

This page presents key statistics and asset details for the 313@somerset property (99-year leasehold, 100% owned) as of 30 June 2025, reporting all financial figures in SGD'000 with gross revenue of S$58.7 million and net lettable area of 288,956 sq ft. The content includes a trade sector breakdown table showing Food & Beverages at 40.5%, a lease expiry profile by NLA and GRI from FY2026 to FY2030, site area metrics (48,200 sq ft), and an artist's impression of an adjacent event space.

This page details the audited Portfolio Statement for the three Grade A commercial buildings in Milan, Italy, as of 30 June 2025, reporting gross revenue of S$18.0 million and net property income of S$13.9 million with an ownership structure of 100% freehold. The asset summary includes key statistics such as a total gross area of approximately 78,873 sq m, committed occupancy of 81.6%, and a valuation of €277.4 million, alongside tenant mix information where the broadcasting sector contributes 89.7% of total income.

This page presents the Financial Performance and Management Fees of SGX REIT for FY2025, featuring Gross Revenue (S\$206.5 million) and Net Property Income (NPI) tables that break down revenue by Jem, 313@somerset, and Sky Complex. The report details a 6.5% year-over-year decline in gross revenue due to upfront supplementary rent recognition, alongside increased property operating expenses and finance costs, while explicitly stating the reporting unit as S\$ million.

This page presents Lendlease REIT's DPU (1.80 cents for both halves of FY2025) and an Assets and Liabilities table reporting total assets at S$3,906,209 thousand and net assets at S$2,147,984 thousand as at 30 June 2025. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as SGD'000 in the table header.

This page presents the Capital Management table with key metrics as at 30 June 2025, including gross borrowings of S$1,664.3 million, a gearing ratio of 42.6%, and an ICR of 1.6 times, alongside narrative details on debt refinancing, sustainability-linked facilities, and asset divestment plans. The reporting unit is explicitly stated as S$ million.

This page presents the Committed Debt Maturity Profile and Liquidity table detailing drawn and undrawn debt facilities in S$ million from FY2026 to FY2030, alongside a cash flow summary reporting net cash generated from operating activities of S$162.6 million and net financing outflows of S$145.0 million for FY2025.

This page presents the "Historic Retail Net Supply (Up to Q2 2025)" and "Upcoming Retail Supply Under Construction (H2 2025 to 2029)" tables reporting net retail supply in '000 sq ft by submarket or period, alongside a market review of new developments and planned areas under URA's Draft Master Plan 2025.

This page presents independent market review data on Singapore's retail property vacancy rates by submarket and micro-market from Q2 2020 to Q2 2025, featuring two tables detailing trends for Central Area, Fringe Area, Suburban, Island-wide, Jurong East, Orchard, and Marine Parade. No audited Portfolio Statement, financial statements, revenue/expenses, tenant lists, trade mix, distribution highlights, or manager information are present; no schema-relevant data.

This page presents retail absorption data for Singapore from Q2 2020 to Q2 2025, featuring a main table titled "Retail Absorption by Submarket (Q2 2020 to Q2 2025)" reporting figures in '000 sq ft across Central Area, Fringe Area, Suburban, and Island-wide segments. Additional tables detail micro-market performance for Jurong East, Orchard, and Marine Parade, with accompanying text highlighting average gross absorption trends and notable F&B and fashion retailer expansions.

This page features a main artifact titled "Retail Capital Values, Net Yields and Transaction Volume" reporting total retail investment volume of S$3.4 billion (S$'000) from Q3 2024 to Q2 2025, alongside Cistri's valuation metrics indicating island-wide yields of 5.0% as at Q2 2025 with specific capital values for Orchard and Suburban submarkets. It details significant transactions including the sale of Concorde Hotel & Shopping Mall for S$821 million and CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust's acquisition of a 50% stake in ION Orchard for S$1.85 billion, while noting stable capital values driven by robust investor interest.

This page presents an Independent Market Review of the Singapore office sector, featuring a table titled "Geographic Distribution of Existing Office Stock in Singapore by Submarket as at Q2 2025 (%)" and a table showing "Historic Net Office Supply by Submarket (Up to Q2 2025) ('000 sq ft)".

This page presents an Independent Market Review summarizing Q2 2025 office market dynamics, featuring two key data tables: "Office Absorption by Submarket (Up to Q2 2025)" and "Office Vacancy by Submarket (Q2 2020 to Q2 2025)". Both tables display submarket performance metrics in '000 sq ft and percentages respectively, sourced from URA and Cistri.

This page presents a table titled "Median Office Rents by Submarket (Q2 2020 to Q2 2025)" reporting quarterly rent data in S$ per sq ft per month for Core CBD, Fringe CBD, and Decentralised submarkets sourced from Cistri.

This page presents the distribution of existing office stock in Milan (Q2 2025) by submarket and a table detailing future new supply ('000 sq m) from 2025 to 2028 across speculative, pre-committed, planned, and total categories. The text further outlines office delivery figures for 2024, projected completions through 2028, and specific details on major upcoming developments including I Portali, Symbiosis, Scalo Farini, and Milan Innovation District.

This page presents a Stacked bar chart titled "Office Absorption by Submarket (2020 to H1 2025)" in '000 sq m, detailing absorption figures for CBD/Centre/Semi-Central, Periphery, and Hinterland submarkets alongside Total Milan. It also includes a Line chart showing Average Office Rents by Submarket (Q2 2020 to Q2 2025) in € per sq m per year, tracking rent trends for Milan CBD and Periphery without any audited financial statements or tenant data.

This page presents an Independent Market Review of the Milan office investment market, featuring a table titled "Office Property Investment Volumes in Milan (2020 to Q2 2025)" with data expressed in € million.

This page presents the Unitholdings by Geography, Investor Type, and Unit Price/Trading Volume for Lendlease REIT's FY2025 period as of 30 June 2025, alongside a Total Return table reporting -15.39% since listing (assuming dividends reinvested). The reporting unit is explicitly stated as S$ per unit for price data and S$ million for market capitalisation.

This page presents trading price performance data for Lendlease Global Commercial REIT and related indices from July 2024 to June 2025, including monthly rebased index values, historical listing performance since October 2019, and combined bar/line charts of trading volume (in million units) and unit price (in S$). No schema-relevant data.

This page discloses quantitative remuneration under AIFMD, reporting total staff remuneration of S$3.05 million for FY2025 and a table of directors' fees in SGD (ranging from S$93,000 to S$157,000). It also details the level and mix of compensation for the CEO and key management personnel with base salaries paid in cash totaling between S$217,577 and S$250,000 for the respective periods.

This page contains corporate governance information detailing the working experience, shareholding interests, and conflict of interest disclosures for directors Mr Justin Marco Gabbani and Mr Simon John Perrott. No schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio statements, financial highlights, or tenant tables are present on this page.

This page contains the table of contents for SGX REIT's financial statements, listing pages 104 through 120 including the Report of the Trustee, Statements of Financial Position, Consolidated Statement of Profit or Loss and Other Comprehensive Income, Consolidated Distribution Statement, and Portfolio Statements. No specific schema-relevant data such as audited portfolio valuations, revenue/expense tables, tenant mix, distribution highlights, or manager/trustee details are present on this page.

This page presents the Independent Auditors' Report on Lendlease Global Commercial REIT's financial statements for the year ended 30 June 2025, confirming that the consolidated statement of financial position, portfolio statement, profit or loss, distribution statement, and other related statements (all reported in SGD'000) present fairly in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. The report details key audit matters regarding the fair value valuation of investment properties in Singapore and Milan as of 30 June 2025, referencing Note 5 to the financial statements but containing no audited Portfolio Statement, revenue/expense tables, tenant mix, or financial highlights.

No schema-relevant data such as audited Portfolio Statements, financial highlights, or tenant mix tables are present.

Key line items include property operating expenses, management fees (base, performance, and other), trustee fees, net finance costs, fair-value changes on investment properties and equity instruments, and total comprehensive income for the year of 83,328.

The statement includes a breakdown of distributions paid per unit for specific periods and Note A which explicitly lists Manager's base fees, performance fees, property manager's fees, and fair-value changes as key adjustments within net tax and other adjustments totaling S$35,153.

The table explicitly lists property locations, land lease terms, remaining lease years, existing uses, and comparative occupancy percentages for 2025 and 2024, while footnotes clarify that carrying values are stated at valuation and include renewal options.

The data shows a consolidated Group carrying value of S$3,761,376 (57.0%) in 2025 compared to S$3,680,250 (57.2%) in 2024, with specific property valuations listed by asset class.

This page presents the audited Portfolio Statement for LREIT, detailing carrying values and percentages of total Unitholders' funds for 2025 and 2024. The report lists property valuations including adjustments for fair-value changes and finance costs, with figures reported in S$'000, showing a final net carrying value of S$1,827,360 for 2025 and S$1,811,647 for 2024.

Key components include adjustments for manager's fees, finance income/expense, fair-value changes on investment properties and derivatives, and changes in trade receivables/payables.

This page presents the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for the year ended 30 June 2025, detailing financing activities including proceeds from loans and borrowings of S\$586,000 (S\$'000), distribution payments totaling S\$91,003 (S\$'000), and a net cash used in financing activities of S\$145,015 (S\$'000). The report also lists significant non-cash transactions involving unit issuances for management fees and distribution reinvestment, with all financial figures reported in SGD'000.
